data.description: 26.1, the release of Tiny Takeover, is a game drop for Java Edition released on March 24, 2026,[1] which adds new textures and models for every baby mob that did not already have a unique model, adds the golden dandelion, makes name tags craftable, makes technical changes, and fixes bugs.

<p><b>26.1</b>, the release of <b><a href="/w/Tiny_Takeover" title="Tiny Takeover">Tiny Takeover</a></b>, is a <a href="/w/Game_drop" title="Game drop">game drop</a> for <i><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a></i> released on March 24, 2026,<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> which adds new textures and models for every baby mob that did not already have a unique model, adds the <a href="/w/Golden_dandelion" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden dandelion">golden dandelion</a>, makes <a href="/w/Name_tag" class="mw-redirect" title="Name tag">name tags</a> craftable, makes technical changes, and fixes bugs.
</p><p>This is the first <i>Java Edition</i> release version to use the <a href="/w/Version_formats#Release" title="Version formats">new "<i>year</i>.<i>drop</i>.<i>hotfix</i>" version format</a> announced in December 2025,<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and to be fully unobfuscated without an accompanying obfuscated variant.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It is the first version released in 2026 and the first to require <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java_version_history#Java_SE_25_.28LTS.29" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:Java version history">Java 25</a>.
</p>

<ul><li>Can also be bought from <a href="/w/Wandering_trader" class="mw-redirect" title="Wandering trader">wandering traders</a>.</li>
<li>When used on a baby mob, it will stop aging. This sets NBT attribute <code>AgeLocked</code> to 1.
<ul><li>When used again, it will continue to age again. This sets NBT attribute <code>AgeLocked</code> to 0.</li></ul></li>
<li>Golden dandelions have different particles depending on if it is used to start or stop aging.
<ul><li>When aging is stopped, green particles moving downwards will be shown.</li>
<li>When aging is started, green particles moving upwards will be shown.</li></ul></li>
<li>Cannot be used on <a href="/w/Monster" title="Monster">monsters</a> (including <a href="/w/Undead_mount" class="mw-redirect" title="Undead mount">undead mounts</a>, but excluding baby <a href="/w/Hoglin" title="Hoglin">hoglins</a>) and <a href="/w/Villager" title="Villager">villagers</a>.</li>
<li>Can be placed and <a href="/w/Flower_Pot" title="Flower Pot">potted</a> like other flowers.</li>
<li>Can be used to craft <a href="/w/Yellow_dye" class="mw-redirect" title="Yellow dye">yellow dye</a> and a <a href="/w/Saturation" class="mw-redirect" title="Saturation">Saturation</a> <a href="/w/Suspicious_stew" class="mw-redirect" title="Suspicious stew">suspicious stew</a>.</li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Command_format">Command format</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?section=3&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Command format" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section's source code: Command format"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><b><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/swing" title="Commands/swing">swing</a></span></code></b>
</p>
<ul><li>New command that enables swinging of entities' arms.</li>
<li>Not all entities support swing animation. <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/swing" title="Commands/swing">swing</a></span></code> will succeed for those entities, but clients will only display it when possible.
<ul><li>For example, this makes it possible to swing mannequin arms.</li></ul></li>
<li>Returns the amount of entities for which a swing was sent.
<ul><li>Syntax: <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/swing" title="Commands/swing">swing</a> <entity selector> <mainhand|offhand></span></code></li></ul></li>
<li>Both arguments can be omitted.
<ul><li>The entity selector will be <code>@s</code> if omitted.</li>
<li>Which hand to swing will be <code>mainhand</code> if omitted.</li></ul></li></ul>

<p><b><a href="/w/Data_component_format" title="Data component format">Data component format</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added <code>minecraft:additional_trade_cost</code>
<ul><li>Transient component used to modify the amount of items wanted in a villager trade.
<ul><li>Removed after a trade has been generated.</li></ul></li>
<li>Format: integer.</li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li>Added <code>minecraft:dye</code>
<ul><li>Represents a color of dye.</li>
<li>Used in various places that previously required the exact dye item, including mob and block interactions.
<ul><li>The presence of this component itself does not enable functionality. The item has to be explicitly allowed for the given functionality, for example by adding it to tags or changing recipe ingredients.</li></ul></li>
<li>Format: one of <code>white</code>, <code>orange</code>, <code>magenta</code>, <code>light_blue</code>, <code>yellow</code>, <code>lime</code>, <code>pink</code>, <code>gray</code>, <code>light_gray</code>, <code>cyan</code>, <code>purple</code>, <code>blue</code>, <code>brown</code>, <code>green</code>, <code>red</code>, <code>black</code></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Villager_trade_definition" title="Villager trade definition">Data-driven villager trades</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Trades offered by <a href="/w/Villager" title="Villager">villagers</a> and <a href="/w/Wandering_trader" class="mw-redirect" title="Wandering trader">wandering traders</a> are now data-driven and can be customized by datapack developers.
<ul><li>Villager Trades
<ul><li>Present in the <code>villager_trade</code> folder, represents a blueprint for trades which is used by villagers and wandering traders to generate actual trades.</li>
<li>Entry Format:
<ul><li><code>wants</code> – an object representing an item type and number of them needed to trade.
<ul><li><code>id</code> – the id of the item</li>
<li><code>count</code> – an optional number provider representing how many of the item is needed for the trade.
<ul><li>Defaults to a constant <code>1</code></li></ul></li>
<li><code>components</code> – an optional component map representing the expected data components on the item.
<ul><li>Defaults to an empty map.</li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><code>additional_wants</code> – an optional object representing an additional item required by the merchant, has the same format as wants.</li>
<li><code>gives</code> – an item Stack representing the resulting item given by the merchant when trading.
<ul><li>Uses the existing format for item stacks.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>given_item_modifiers</code> – a optional list of item Modifiers representing modifiers to apply to the item in gives such as enchantments or potions, used to add dynamism to the trade rather than hardcoding certain values.
<ul><li>Uses the existing format for item modifiers (also known as loot modifiers, item functions, loot functions...).</li>
<li>If any of these returns an empty item the entire trade will be discarded.</li>
<li>Item Modifier references are not supported.</li>
<li>If the final item has a <code>stored_enchantment</code> component containing an enchantment in the <code>#double_trade_price</code> tag, then the count of <code>wants</code> is doubled.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>max_uses</code> – an optional number provider representing the maximum number of times a trade may be used.
<ul><li>Is set to <code>1</code> if the number provider returns a lower value.</li>
<li>Defaults to <code>4</code></li></ul></li>
<li><code>reputation_discount</code> – a– number provider representing how much factors such as demand, discounts or penalties affects the cost represented by wants.
<ul><li>Is set to <code>0.0</code> if the number provider returns a lower value.</li>
<li>Defaults to <code>0.0</code></li></ul></li>
<li><code>xp</code> – an optional number provider representing the amount of xp a merchant gets when the trade is done.
<ul><li>Is set to <code>0</code> if the number provider returns a lower value.</li>
<li>Defaults to <code>1</code></li></ul></li>
<li><code>merchant_predicate</code> – a predicate representing conditions on the merchant that need to be met for the trade to be offered.
<ul><li>Uses the existing format for predicates.</li>
<li>Predicate references are not supported.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>double_trade_price_enchantments</code> – an optional enchantment id, list of namespaced enchantment IDs, or hash-prefixed enchantment tag representing enchantments that will double the additional cost from <code>minecraft:enchant_randomly</code> and <code>minecraft:enchant_with_levels</code> if they have <code>include_additional_cost_component</code> set to <code>true</code> and if the item has one of the provided values in its <code>minecraft:stored_enchantments</code> component.</li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li>An example trade of an emerald and a book for an enchanted book offered only by desert villagers.</li></ul></li></ul>
<div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-json mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr"><pre><span></span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"additional_wants"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:book"</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">},</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"double_trade_price_enchantments"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"#minecraft:double_trade_price"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"given_item_modifiers"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">"function"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:enchant_randomly"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">"include_additional_cost_component"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">"only_compatible"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">"options"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"#minecraft:trades/desert_common"</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">},</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">"function"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:filtered"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">"item_filter"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">"items"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:enchanted_book"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">"predicates"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">"minecraft:stored_enchantments"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">            </span><span class="p">{}</span>
<span class="w">          </span><span class="p">]</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="p">},</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">"on_fail"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">"function"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:discard"</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">],</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"gives"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"count"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:enchanted_book"</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">},</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"max_uses"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">12.0</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"merchant_predicate"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"condition"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:entity_properties"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"entity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"this"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"predicate"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">"predicates"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">"minecraft:villager/variant"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:desert"</span>
<span class="w">      </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">},</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"reputation_discount"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.2</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"wants"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:emerald"</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</pre></div>
<p><b>Entity <a href="/w/Tag_(Java_Edition)" title="Tag (Java Edition)">tags</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added <code>#cannot_be_age_locked</code>
<ul><li>Defines which baby mobs that age that can not have its aging stopped using a <a href="/w/Golden_dandelion" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden dandelion">golden dandelion</a>.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Environment_attribute" title="Environment attribute">Environment attributes</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:visual/block_light_tint</code>
<ul><li>Tint of the block light. Block light color start as dark grey at low light levels, becomes tinted by this attribute at medium levels and turns white at high levels. By default, it provides the yellowish tint of torches. Bright colors work best for this attribute, with at least one color component being fully bright. The tint applies globally to all light sources visible on the screen. Individual lights can not be tinted differently.</li>
<li>Value type: RGB color</li>
<li>Default value: <span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: #FFD88C; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> #FFD88C</span></li>
<li>Modifiers: RGB Color Modifiers</li>
<li>Interpolated: yes</li>
<li>Resolved at the camera's position</li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:visual/ambient_light_color</code>
<ul><li>Defines both the ambient light tint and brightness. This light is applied to the world at 0 light level. Block and sky light are added on top of it.</li>
<li>Value type: RGB color</li>
<li>Default value: <span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: #000000; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> #000000</span>.</li>
<li>Modifiers: RGB Color Modifiers</li>
<li>Interpolated: yes</li>
<li>Resolved at the camera's position.</li>
<li>Set to <span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: #0A0A0A; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> #0A0A0A</span> in the Overworld, <span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: #302821; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> #302821</span> in the Nether, and <span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: #3f473f; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> #3f473f</span> in the End.</li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:visual/night_vision_color</code>
<ul><li>This color is used similarly to ambient light color. When the Night Vision effect is active, per-component maximum of <code>minecraft:visual/night_vision_color</code> and <code>minecraft:visual/ambient_light_color</code> is used as ambient color. <a href="/w/Night_Vision" title="Night Vision">Night Vision</a> is not tinted by default.</li>
<li>Value type: RGB color</li>
<li>Default value: <span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: #999999; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> #999999</span></li>
<li>Modifiers: RGB Color Modifiers</li>
<li>Interpolated: yes</li>
<li>Resolved at the camera's position</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b>Fluid <a href="/w/Tag_(Java_Edition)" title="Tag (Java Edition)">tags</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added tags to determine which fluids can support the following blocks:
<ul><li><code>#supports_lily_pad</code></li>
<li><code>#supports_frogspawn</code></li></ul></li>

<p><b>Item <a href="/w/Tag_(Java_Edition)" title="Tag (Java Edition)">tags</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added <code>#metal_nuggets</code>
<ul><li>Contains all types of <a href="/w/Nugget" title="Nugget">nuggets</a>.</li></ul></li>
<li>Added <code>#dyes</code>
<ul><li>Contains all vanilla <a href="/w/Dye" title="Dye">dyes</a>.</li></ul></li>
<li>Added <code>#loom_dyes</code>
<ul><li>Contains all items that are allowed in the Loom screen to set pattern colors.</li>

<li>Added <code>#loom_patterns</code>

<li>The loom screen also requires the <code>minecraft:provides_banner_patterns</code> component to be present on item stacks.</li></ul></li>
<li>Added <code>#cat_collar_dyes</code>
<ul><li>Contains all items that can be used to dye a pet cat's collar.</li>
<li>The color will be taken from the <code>minecraft:dye</code> component of the used item stack.</li></ul></li>
<li>Added <code>#wolf_collar_dyes</code>
<ul><li>Contains all items that can be used to dye a pet wolf's collar.</li>
<li>The color will be taken from the <code>minecraft:dye</code> component of the used item stack.</li></ul></li>
<li>Added <code>#cauldron_can_remove_dye</code>
<ul><li>Contains all items that can be used on water-filled cauldron to remove <code>minecraft:dyed_color</code> component.</li></ul></li>
<li>Added the following tags which mirror their block tag contents:
<ul><li><code>#mud</code></li>
<li><code>#moss_blocks</code></li>
<li><code>#grass_blocks</code></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b>Lightmap debug renderer</b>
</p>
<ul><li>A new debug renderer for the lightmap was added, which can be enabled using the <kbd class="key nowrap">F3</kbd> + <kbd class="key nowrap">4</kbd> keybind.</li>
<li>It is mutually exclusive with FPS/TPS and networking charts.</li>
<li>It shows the lightmap texture in real-time in the bottom right corner of the screen.</li>
<li>The vertical axis of the texture represent sky light levels (0-15 from bottom to top).</li>
<li>The horizontal axis of the texture represent block light levels (0-15 from left to right).</li>
<li>The color of each pixel represents the resulting color that will be applied to blocks and entities lit with the corresponding block and sky light levels.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Loot_context" title="Loot context">Loot contexts</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added <code>minecraft:villager_trade</code> which takes the following parameters:
<ul><li><code>this</code> – the entity offering the trade.</li>
<li><code>origin</code> – the block position of the entity at its feet.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Loot_functions" class="mw-redirect" title="Loot functions">Loot functions</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added <code>minecraft:set_random_dyes</code>
<ul><li>Additively adds dyes to an item's <code>minecraft:dyed_color</code> data component:</li>
<li><code>conditions</code> – conditions for the function to apply.</li>
<li><code>number_of_dyes</code> – number provider representing the number of random dyes out of sixteen to apply to the item.
<ul><li>The same dye might be selected repeatedly.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li>Added <code>minecraft:set_random_potion</code>
<ul><li>Randomly sets the minecraft:potion_contents data component on an item Fields:</li>
<li><code>conditions</code> – conditions for the function to apply.</li>
<li><code>options</code> – optional potion id, list of namespaced potion IDs, or hash-prefixed potion tag, representing the possible potions to select from.
<ul><li>Defaults to any potion in the potions registry.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Number_provider" class="mw-redirect" title="Number provider">Number providers</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added <code>minecraft:environment_attribute</code>
<ul><li>Fetches and provides the value of an <a href="/w/Environment_attribute" title="Environment attribute">environment attribute</a> (that can be represented as a number).
<ul><li>This provider requires a context with an <code>origin</code> position set as long as the <a href="/w/Environment_attribute" title="Environment attribute">environment attribute</a> can vary positionally.</li></ul></li>
<li>Format: object with fields:
<ul><li><code>attribute</code> – <a href="/w/Environment_attribute" title="Environment attribute">environment attribute</a> ID to fetch.</li>
<li>e.g. <code>{type: 'environment_attribute', attribute: 'gameplay/sky_light_level'}</code></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li>Added <code>minecraft:sum</code>
<ul><li>Returns the sum of a list of number providers.</li>
<li>Fields:
<ul><li><code>summands</code> – a list of number providers.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Options" title="Options">Options</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added a new display option called "Exclusive Fullscreen" which controls if fullscreen mode should take full control of a monitor.
<ul><li>Defaults to <code>false</code> (i.e. non-exclusive mode).</li>
<li>Any change will be applied only after the game restarts.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Particles_(Java_Edition)" class="mw-redirect" title="Particles (Java Edition)">Particles</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added <code>pause_mob_growth</code>
<ul><li>Particles showing on a baby mob which has had its aging stopped using a <a href="/w/Golden_dandelion" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden dandelion">golden dandelion</a>.</li></ul></li>
<li>Added <code>reset_mob_growth</code>
<ul><li>Particles showing on a baby mob which has had its aging reset and started using a <a href="/w/Golden_dandelion" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden dandelion">golden dandelion</a>.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b>Potion <a href="/w/Tag_(Java_Edition)" title="Tag (Java Edition)">tags</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added <code>#tradeable</code>
<ul><li>Contains all potion effects that can appear in villager trades.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Predicate" title="Predicate">Predicates</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added the <code>minecraft:environment_attribute_check</code> loot predicate.
<ul><li>Exactly matches the value of an <a href="/w/Environment_attribute" title="Environment attribute">environment attribute</a> at a given position.
<ul><li>This predicate requires a context with an <code>origin</code> position set as long as the <a href="/w/Environment_attribute" title="Environment attribute">environment attribute</a> can vary positionally.</li></ul></li>
<li>Format: object with fields:
<ul><li><code>attribute</code> – <a href="/w/Environment_attribute" title="Environment attribute">environment attribute</a> ID to test</li>
<li><code>value</code> – Exact value of the <a href="/w/Environment_attribute" title="Environment attribute">environment attribute</a> to match</li>
<li>e.g. <code>{condition: 'environment_attribute_check', attribute: 'gameplay/piglins_zombify', value: true}</code></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Time_marker" class="mw-redirect" title="Time marker">Time markers</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Time markers assign a particular name to a specific (optionally repeating) point in time for a specific world clock. Time markers replace the previously predetermined names that could be used by <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> set</span></code>, for example <code>day</code> or <code>night</code></li>
<li>Time markers will exist within the context of a specific world clock. This means that even though the different time markers are defined by different Timelines, only one Time Marker can exist with a particular id for a particular world clock. It also means that two world clocks can have a time marker with the same name.
<ul><li>Built-in uses of time markers
<ul><li>Some time markers are used to drive Vanilla game behavior. Usually, they are configured to not show up in <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a></span></code> commands.
<ul><li><code>minecraft:wake_up_from_sleep</code> – the time to advance the dimension's default clock to when players in that dimension wake up after sleeping.</li>
<li><code>minecraft:roll_village_siege</code> – the time of the dimension's default clock at which the random chance for a zombie village siege to occur should be evaluated.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Trade_sets" class="mw-redirect" title="Trade sets">Trade sets</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>What trades are unlocked by villager professions are now determined using deterministic random sequences, like loot drops and barter loot.</li>
<li>Present in the <code>trade_set</code> folder, they are groupings of trades offered by <a href="/w/Villager" title="Villager">villagers</a> and <a href="/w/Wandering_traders" class="mw-redirect" title="Wandering traders">wandering traders</a>.</li>
<li>Currently only hardcoded ones are available in <code><profession>/level_<level></code> for villagers, as well as <code>wandering_trader/buying</code>, <code>wandering_trader/special</code>, <code>wandering_trader/common</code> for wandering traders.</li>
<li>Entry Format:
<ul><li><code>trades</code>, a villager trade id, list of namespaced villager trade IDs, or hash-prefixed villager trade tag representing the trades that are part of this trade set.</li>
<li><code>amount</code>, a number provider representing the amount of trades to be generated from this set when used.
<ul><li>If the generated number is greater than the number of available <code>trades</code> then it will only generate until all <code>trades</code> have been used once, unless <code>allow_duplicates</code> is set to <code>true</code></li></ul></li>
<li><code>allow_duplicates</code>, a boolean representing if the trade set can use the same villager trade multiple times to generate trades.
<ul><li>Defaults to <code>false</code></li></ul></li>
<li><code>random_sequence</code>, an optional named random sequence that determines which trades are generated.
<ul><li>Defaults to a non-deterministic random sequence.</li></ul></li>
<li>An example trade set offering 2 trades from the <code>#minecraft:armorer/level_1</code> tag, allowing duplicates.</li></ul></li></ul>
<div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-json mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr"><pre><span></span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">"amount"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">2.0</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">"trades"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"#minecraft:armorer/level_1"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">"random_sequence"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:trade_set/armorer/level_1"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">"allow_duplicates"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</pre></div>
<p><b>Villager Trade <a href="/w/Tag_(Java_Edition)" title="Tag (Java Edition)">tags</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added several tags representing groups of villager trades from which <a href="/w/Villager" title="Villager">villagers</a> and <a href="/w/Wandering_trader" class="mw-redirect" title="Wandering trader">wandering traders</a> derive their trading pools.
<ul><li>Villagers have the following tags representing each profession and level of trade in the format: <code>#<profession>/level_<level></code>, up to level 5.
<ul><li>Smiths have the <code>#common_smith/level_<level></code> tags representing common trades among armorers, weaponsmiths and toolsmiths, up to level 5.</li></ul></li>
<li>Wandering Traders have the following tags: <code>#wandering_trader/buying</code>, <code>#wandering_trader/special</code>, <code>#wandering_trader/common</code>.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/World_clock" class="mw-redirect" title="World clock">World clocks</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Each world clock contains an internal time that increases every tick. A world clock can be defined in data packs under the <code>world_clock</code> registry (i.e. found under <samp>data/<namespace>/world_clock/<id>.json</samp>)</li>
<li>A world clock can be paused or resumed, and the time of the clock can be changed or queried, using the <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a></span></code> command.
<ul><li>This allows different <a href="/w/Dimension_definition" title="Dimension definition">dimensions</a> to have different clocks.</li></ul></li>
<li>Format: object with no fields</li>
<li>Added <code>minecraft:the_end</code> world clock to <a href="/w/The_End" title="The End">the End</a> dimension.
<ul><li>It now controls <a href="/w/End_flashes" class="mw-redirect" title="End flashes">End flashes</a>.</li></ul></li></ul>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Blocks_2">Blocks</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?section=6&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Blocks" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section's source code: Blocks"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><b><a href="/w/Dispenser" title="Dispenser">Dispenser</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/w/Spawn_egg" class="mw-redirect" title="Spawn egg">Spawn egg</a> without an <a href="/w/Data_component#entity_data" class="mw-redirect" title="Data component"><code>entity_data</code></a> component are dropped as an item. Previously, the dispenser failed to activate.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Note_block" class="mw-redirect" title="Note block">Note block</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added the trumpet instrument.
<ul><li>It can be heard when a note block is placed on top of a <a href="/w/Block_of_copper" class="mw-redirect" title="Block of copper">block of copper</a>.</li>
<li>The sound is different based on the oxidation level of the copper block.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Stonecutter" title="Stonecutter">Stonecutter</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/w/Deepslate" title="Deepslate">Deepslate</a> can now be directly crafted into its <a href="/w/Cobbled_Deepslate" title="Cobbled Deepslate">cobbled</a>, <a href="/w/Polished_Deepslate" title="Polished Deepslate">polished</a>, <a href="/w/Deepslate_Bricks" title="Deepslate Bricks">brick</a>, and <a href="/w/Deepslate_Tile" class="mw-redirect" title="Deepslate Tile">tile</a> variants in the stonecutter.</li>
<li><a href="/w/Stone" title="Stone">Stone</a> can now be directly crafted into its <a href="/w/Cobblestone" title="Cobblestone">cobblestone</a> variants in the stonecutter.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Tripwire" class="mw-redirect" title="Tripwire">Tripwire</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The tripwire texture is now rendered as alpha cutout instead of transparent. In other words, the texture is now opaque thus making tripwire easier to see.</li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Items">Items</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?section=7&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Items" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section's source code: Items"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><b><a href="/w/Bundle" title="Bundle">Bundles</a> </b>
</p>
<ul><li>Now supports a <a href="/w/Data_component#bundle_container" class="mw-redirect" title="Data component"><code>bundle_contents</code></a> component with a weight greater than 2<sup>31</sup>-1, equivalent to 2<sup>31</sup>-1 stacks.
<ul><li>Previously, the component was removed when the limit was exceeded.</li>
<li>A bundle exceeding this limit is shown as full, however, when attempting to empty it, add a new item, or view the tooltip, it still appears empty.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b> <a href="/w/Item_stack" class="mw-redirect" title="Item stack">Item stack</a> </b>
</p>
<ul><li>Now, in many cases, it is treated as empty if it has conflicting data, such as having a count greater than <a href="/w/Data_component#max_stack_size" class="mw-redirect" title="Data component"><code>max_stack_size</code></a>, or having <code>max_stack_size</code> greater than one along with <a href="/w/Data_component#max_damage" class="mw-redirect" title="Data component"><code>max_damage</code></a>.
<ul><li>When mining a <a href="/w/Shulker_box" class="mw-redirect" title="Shulker box">shulker box</a> containing an item stack with a conflicting data, it will treat the item as <code>Air x0</code> in the tooltip, and placing it in a block the item stack will be removed.</li>
<li>Shooting an <a href="/w/Arrow" title="Arrow">arrow</a> with a conflicting data using a <a href="/w/Crossbow" title="Crossbow">crossbow</a> will not be a project.</li>
<li><span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">Using</span> a <a href="/w/Bundle" title="Bundle">bundle</a> to remove an item stack with a conflicting data, no items will be dropped.</li>
<li>Item stacks with conflicting data can still be placed in <a href="/w/Chest" title="Chest">chests</a> and in the <a href="/w/Inventory" title="Inventory">inventory</a>.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Name_tag" class="mw-redirect" title="Name tag">Name tag</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Can now be crafted with 1 paper and 1 <a href="/w/Nugget" title="Nugget">nugget</a>.</li></ul>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Command_format_2">Command format</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?section=10&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Command format" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section's source code: Command format"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><b><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/fetchprofile" title="Commands/fetchprofile">fetchprofile</a></span></code></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added a new entity subcommand that will print profile information from entity in world.
<ul><li>Syntax: <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/fetchprofile" title="Commands/fetchprofile">fetchprofile</a> entity <single entity selector></span></code></li>
<li>If targeted entity does not have profile (currently only Players and Mannequins do) this command will fail.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a></span></code></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a></span></code> command is now based on world clocks.
<ul><li>A clock can be optionally specified as an input for the time command with <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> of <clock> ...</span></code>.</li>
<li>If the clock is not specified (<code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> ...</span></code> as before), the default clock for the dimension is used.</li></ul></li>
<li>The return value (e.g. from <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/execute" title="Commands/execute">execute</a> store</span></code>) from the <code>set</code> and <code>add</code> subcommands is now the total elapsed ticks of the clock instead of the current time of day.</li>
<li>Syntax:
<ul><li><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> [of <clock>] set <time></span></code> – sets the total elapsed ticks of the clock.</li>
<li><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> [of <clock>] set <timemarker></span></code> – advances the clock forward to the next occurrence of the time marker.
<ul><li>For the <code>minecraft:overworld</code> clock, the available time markers are: <code>day</code>, <code>noon</code>, <code>night</code>, and <code>midnight</code></li></ul></li>
<li><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> [of <clock>] add <time></span></code> – adds ticks to the clock, can be a negative or a positive number.</li>
<li><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> [of <clock>] pause</span></code> – pauses the clock.</li>
<li><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> [of <clock>] resume</span></code> – resumes the clock.</li>
<li><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> [of <clock>] query <timeline></span></code> – displays and returns the current number of ticks within the timeline's period.</li>
<li><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> [of <clock>] query <timeline> repetition</span></code> – displays and returns the number of times the timeline's period has repeated.</li>
<li><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> [of <clock>] query time</span></code> – displays and returns the total elapsed ticks of the clock.</li>
<li><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> query gametime</span></code> – as before, the total elapsed ticks within the world (unaffected by changes made to clocks using <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a></span></code>).</li>
<li><code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a> [of <clock>] rate <rate></span></code> – sets the rate multiplier at which the clock should advance.
<ul><li>This only changes the rate at which the <a href="/w/World_clock" class="mw-redirect" title="World clock">world clock</a> and any <a href="/w/Timeline" title="Timeline">timelines</a> dependent on it advance their internal timers.
<ul><li>For example, in the case of the <code>minecraft:overworld</code> clock, the day/night cycle will pass quicker with a larger value, but actual game simulation will not speed up (as would happen with <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/tick" title="Commands/tick">tick</a> rate</span></code>).</li></ul></li>
<li>A <code>rate</code> of <code>1</code> corresponds to normal speed.</li>
<li><code>rate</code> is a float between <code>0</code> (exclusive) and <code>1000</code> (inclusive).</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Gameplay">Gameplay</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?section=11&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Gameplay" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section's source code: Gameplay"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><b><a href="/w/Trading" title="Trading">Trading</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The master librarian no longer offers <a href="/w/Name_tag" class="mw-redirect" title="Name tag">name tags</a>.</li>
<li>The master librarian will now offer <a href="/w/Red_candle" class="mw-redirect" title="Red candle">red candles</a> and <a href="/w/Yellow_candle" class="mw-redirect" title="Yellow candle">yellow candles</a> for the price of three <a href="/w/Emerald" title="Emerald">emeralds</a>.</li>
<li>The <a href="/w/Wandering_trader" class="mw-redirect" title="Wandering trader">wandering trader</a> will now offer <a href="/w/Name_tag" class="mw-redirect" title="Name tag">name tags</a> for the price of one emerald.</li>
<li>The master <a href="/w/Librarian" title="Librarian">librarian</a> will now have three available trades to ensure that an enchanted book trade is always offered when using the <a href="/w/Villager_Trade_Rebalance" title="Villager Trade Rebalance">Villager Trade Rebalance</a> experiment.</li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="General_2">General</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?section=12&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: General" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_26.1?action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section's source code: General"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><b>General</b>
</p>
<ul><li>If a server's disk space is low, a toast will now be shown to server operators.</li>
<li>The game now requires Java 25.</li>
<li>The included Java distribution is now the Microsoft build of OpenJDK 25.</li>
<li>Tweaked default JVM options.
<ul><li>The game now allocates 4 GB of RAM by default (up from 2 GB).</li>
<li>Garbage collection has been changed from G1GC to ZGC for compatible computers.​<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><a href="/w/Special:TalkPage/Java_Edition_26.1" title="Special:TalkPage/Java Edition 26.1"><span title="Which hardware/software configuration is needed for ZGC to be enabled by default?" style="border-bottom: 1px dotted">more information needed</span></a></i>]</sup></li></ul></li>
<li>Added <code>-XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch -XX:+UseStringDeduplication</code> to the default JVM arguments.</li>
<li>Changed the internals of how chunk geometry data is stored in GPU memory and how they are rendered.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Block_model" class="mw-redirect" title="Block model">Block model</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Any block model can now support cutout or translucent (partially transparent pixels) textures.
<ul><li>Whether a quad is rendered in the cutout or translucent render pass is determined by the contents of its assigned sprite.
<ul><li>Any sprite with translucent (partially transparent) pixels will be assigned to the "translucent" pass.</li>
<li>Any sprite with fully transparent pixels will be assigned to the "cutout" pass.</li>
<li>All other sprites are assigned to the "solid" pass.</li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li>The format of the <code>textures</code> map has been updated:
<ul><li>Non-string entries will now be rejected, instead of interpreted as strings.</li>
<li>Alongside the previous inline sprite ID form, entries can now be defined as an object with fields:
<ul><li><code>sprite</code> – the sprite ID</li>
<li><code>force_translucent</code> – optional boolean, <code>true</code> if any geometry with this texture should be forced into the "translucent" pass.
<ul><li>This is useful for example for blocks that don't have any translucent pixels, but use the <code>mean</code> mipmap strategy.</li>
<li>Default: <code>false</code></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Block_states" title="Block states">Block states</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The <code>rotation</code> property in default block state of <a href="/w/Banner" title="Banner">banners</a> and <a href="/w/Sign" title="Sign">signs</a> has been changed from <code>0</code> to <code>8</code></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Chat" title="Chat">Chat</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The chat screen can now always be opened, even when chatting is restricted by settings.
<ul><li>When the chat screen is open, specific actions and message types may still be restricted.</li>
<li>Information about the restrictions (if there are any) is displayed on top of the chat box and above the chat input when the chat screen is open.</li>
<li>The same information can also be accessed in World Settings screen.</li></ul></li>
<li>Chat entries from client actions like taking screenshots will now be displayed even when messages from players and servers are restricted.</li>
<li>Changing chat settings will now hide all messages of restricted types and discard any new ones.</li>
<li>The handling of chat messages on a published local server is now more consistent with dedicated servers in regard to chat settings.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Creative" title="Creative">Creative</a> mode</b>
</p>
<ul><li>Using Ctrl + Pick input as an operator on players and mannequins will now show the same results as executing the <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/fetchprofile" title="Commands/fetchprofile">fetchprofile</a></span></code>.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Data_component_format" title="Data component format">Data component format</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:provides_banner_patterns</code>
<ul><li>The component now also accepts an ID or a list of IDs in addition to a tag.</li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:blocks_attacks</code>
<ul><li>The field <code>bypassed_by</code> now also accepts an ID or a list of IDs in addition to a tag.</li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:damage_resistant</code>
<ul><li>The field types now also accepts an ID or a list of IDs in addition to a tag.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Data_pack" title="Data pack">Data pack</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The <a href="/w/Pack_format" title="Pack format">pack format</a> version is now <code>101.1</code>.</li>
<li>The "Default Components" report generator no longer outputs files for entries without any components.</li>
<li>Villager inventory slots can now be accessed using <code>mob.inventory.*</code>; <code>villager.*</code> has been removed.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Debug_screen" title="Debug screen">Debug screen</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added a new entry called <code>detailed_memory</code> with additional information about used memory.</li>
<li>The <code>looking_at_block</code> and <code>looking_at_fluid</code> debug entries no longer show tags.</li>
<li>The <code>day_count</code> debug entry has been split from <code>local_difficulty</code>.</li>
<li>New debug entries have been added:
<ul><li><code>looking_at_block_tags</code></li>
<li><code>looking_at_fluid_tags</code></li>
<li><code>looking_at_entity_tags</code></li></ul></li>
<li>Renamed debug entries:
<ul><li><code>looking_at_block</code> → <code>looking_at_block_state</code></li>
<li><code>looking_at_fluid</code> → <code>looking_at_fluid_state</code></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Dimension_type" title="Dimension type">Dimension types</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added the field <code>default_clock</code>: optional <a href="/w/World_clock" class="mw-redirect" title="World clock">world clock</a> ID.
<ul><li>Specifies the default clock that will be used for the <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/time" title="Commands/time">time</a></span></code> command.
<ul><li>If a default clock is specified, the time command requires an explicit clock argument.</li></ul></li>
<li>Also specifies the clock to which <code>minecraft:wake_up_from_sleep</code> and <code>minecraft:roll_village_siege</code> time markers apply.
<ul><li>If not specified, those time markers will never apply in that dimension.</li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li>Added the field <code>has_ender_dragon_fight</code>: boolean
<ul><li>Controls whether it is possible for an ender dragon fight to exist in the dimension.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Enchantment_definition" title="Enchantment definition">Enchantment definition</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The <code>post_piercing_attack</code> component no longer only works for a player if that player has a certain food level.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Entity_data" class="mw-redirect" title="Entity data">Entity data</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The <code>current_explosion_impact_pos</code> and <code>current_impulse_context_reset_grace_time</code> fields from players have been added to all mobs and the <a href="/w/Armor_stand" class="mw-redirect" title="Armor stand">armor stand</a>.</li>
<li>The <code>ignore_fall_damage_from_current_explosion</code> field on players has been removed.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Environment_attribute" title="Environment attribute">Environment attribute</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Updated the <code>gameplay/turtle_egg_hatch_chance</code> environment attribute to have a default value of <code>0.002</code>.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Game_rule" title="Game rule">Game rules</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The game rules screen is now accessible in-game through a new World Options screen in the pause menu.</li>
<li>A search bar has been added to the top of the game rules screen, both in-game and in the world creation menu.
<ul><li>The search bar also selects game rules based on description and category in addition to namespaced ID and name.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Game_Test" class="mw-redirect" title="Game Test">Game Tests</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Replaced <code>time_of_day</code> with <code>clock_time</code>.
<ul><li>Added a new required field <code>clock</code>: world clock ID, the clock within which to set time (from the existing time field).</li></ul></li>
<li>Added <code>timeline_attributes</code> definitions to set any number of timelines.
<ul><li><code>timelines</code>: A list of timelines to set.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Items_model_definition" title="Items model definition">Items model definition</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The <code>minecraft:model</code>, <code>minecraft:special</code>, <code>minecraft:range_dispatch</code>, <code>minecraft:composite</code>, <code>minecraft:select</code>, <code>minecraft:condition</code> item model types now have <code>transformation</code> fields.
<ul><li>Those fields have the same format as the <code>transformation</code> field on the <code>minecraft:display</code> entity, i.e. either an array of 16 numbers representing a matrix or structure with decomposed translation, scale and rotation info.</li>
<li>For types with children (<code>minecraft:range_dispatch</code>, <code>minecraft:composite</code>, <code>minecraft:select</code>, <code>minecraft:condition</code>), the transformation will be composed with the transformation of the children, except for <code>minecraft:bundle/selected_item</code>.</li>
<li>Model transformations will be applied after item display transformations (i.e. display section in model files).</li></ul></li>
<li>The transformations for some special item models (types referenced by the <code>minecraft:special</code> item model) have been extracted to item models itself.
<ul><li>Affected special model types:
<ul><li><code>minecraft:bed</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:banner</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:conduit</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:copper_golem_statue</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:head</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:player_head</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:shulker_box</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:shield</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:trident</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:standing_sign</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:hanging_sign</code></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li>Special model type
<ul><li><code>minecraft:bell</code>
<ul><li>New special model type that renders the animated part of a <a href="/w/Bell" title="Bell">bell</a> block.</li>
<li>No fields.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>minecraft:book</code>
<ul><li>New special model type that renders a book that normally is a part of <a href="/w/Enchanting_table" class="mw-redirect" title="Enchanting table">enchanting table</a> and <a href="/w/Lectern" title="Lectern">lectern</a>.</li>
<li>Fields:
<ul><li><code>open_angle</code> – angle (in degrees) between book cover and book centerline (<code>0</code> means closed, <code>90</code> means open flat).</li>

<ul><li><code>part</code> – one of: <code>head</code>, <code>foot</code></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><code>minecraft:banner</code>
<ul><li>New field:
<ul><li><code>attachment</code> – selects a model to be used, one of <code>wall</code>, <code>ground</code></li>

<li><code>minecraft:chest</code>
<ul><li>New field:
<ul><li><code>chest_type</code> – selects a model to be used, one of <code>single</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code></li>
<li>Default: <code>single</code></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><code>minecraft:end_cube</code>
<ul><li>New special model type that renders a <a href="/w/Starfield" title="Starfield">starfield</a> cube.
<ul><li>Fields:
<ul><li><code>effect</code> – texture effect to apply, one of: <code>portal</code>, <code>gateway</code></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><code>minecraft:hanging_sign</code>
<ul><li>New field:
<ul><li><code>attachment</code> – selects a model to be used, one of <code>wall</code>, <code>ceiling</code>, <code>ceiling_middle</code></li>
<li>Default: <code>ceiling_middle</code></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><code>minecraft:standing_sign</code>
<ul><li>New field:
<ul><li><code>attachment</code> – selects a model to be used, one of <code>wall</code>, <code>ground</code></li>
<li>Default: <code>ground</code></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><code>minecraft:shulker_box</code>
<ul><li>Removed the <code>orientation</code> field.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Java_Edition_level_format" title="Java Edition level format">level.dat</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The <code>Player</code> tag has been replaced with a <code>singleplayer_uuid</code> tag, referencing the player data file to use.</li>
<li>Difficulty-related settings have been moved into a <code>difficulty_settings</code> tag.
<ul><li>Difficulty is renamed to difficulty and is now a string instead of an integer.
<ul><li>Allowed values:

<li><code>easy</code></li>
<li><code>normal</code></li>
<li><code>hard</code></li></ul></li></ul></li>

<li>Data for the ender dragon fight has been moved out to the <code>data</code> folder.
<ul><li>It can now be found at <samp>dimensions/minecraft/the_end/data/minecraft/ender_dragon_fight.dat</samp></li>
<li>The ender dragon fight can be activated in other dimensions.</li>
<li>Data changes:
<ul><li><code>NeedsStateScanning</code> has been renamed to <code>needs_state_scanning</code></li>
<li><code>DragonKilled</code> has been renamed to <code>dragon_killed</code></li>
<li><code>PreviouslyKilled</code> has been renamed to <code>previously_killed</code></li>

<ul><li>Allowed values:
<ul><li><code>start</code></li>
<li><code>preparing_to_summon_pillars</code></li>
<li><code>summoning_pillars</code></li>
<li><code>summoning_dragon</code></li>
<li><code>end</code></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><code>Dragon</code> has been renamed to <code>dragon_uuid</code></li>
<li><code>ExitPortalLocation</code> has been renamed to <code>exit_portal_location</code></li>
<li><code>Gateways</code> has been renamed to <code>gateways</code></li>
<li>Added <code>respawn_time</code>
<ul><li>The time that has elapsed since the current stage of the respawn sequence started.</li></ul></li>
<li>Added <code>respawn_crystals</code></li>
<li>A list of UUIDs for the end crystals used to trigger the respawn sequence.</li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li>Wandering Trader data has been moved out to the <code>data</code> folder.
<ul><li>It can now be found at <samp>data/minecraft/wandering_trader.dat</samp></li>

<ul><li>It can now be found at <samp>data/minecraft/custom_boss_events.dat</samp></li></ul></li>
<li>Weather-related data has been moved to the <code>data</code> folder.
<ul><li>It can now be found at <samp>data/minecraft/weather.dat</samp></li>

<ul><li><code>clearWeatherTime</code> has been renamed to <code>clear_weather_time</code></li>
<li><code>rainTime</code> has been renamed to <code>rain_time</code></li>
<li><code>thunderTime</code> has been renamed to <code>thunder_time</code></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><code>ScheduledEvents</code> has been moved out to the <code>data</code> folder.
<ul><li>It can now be found at <samp>data/minecraft/scheduled_events.dat</samp></li>
<li>Data changes:
<ul><li><code>Name</code> has been renamed to <code>id</code></li>
<li><code>TriggerTime</code> has been renamed to <code>trigger_time</code></li>
<li><code>Callback</code> has been renamed to <code>callback</code>
<ul><li><code>Type</code> has been renamed to <code>type</code></li>
<li><code>Name</code> has been renamed to <code>id</code></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><code>game_rules</code> has been moved out to the <code>data</code> folder.
<ul><li>It can now be found at <samp>data/minecraft/game_rules.dat</samp></li></ul></li>
<li><code>WorldGenSettings</code> has been moved out to the <code>data</code> folder.
<ul><li>It can now be found at <samp>data/minecraft/world_gen_settings.dat</samp></li>
<li>Data changes:
<ul><li><code>generate_features</code> has been renamed to <code>generate_structures</code></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><code>world_clocks</code> has been moved out to the <code>data</code> folder.
<ul><li>It can now be found at <samp>data/minecraft/world_clocks.dat</samp></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Java_Edition_level_format" title="Java Edition level format">Level format</a></b>
</p>

</div>
<ul><li>All default dimensions are now stored in the <samp><code>dimensions</code></samp> subfolder.
<ul><li>Data for the <a href="/w/Overworld" title="Overworld">Overworld</a> has been moved from the root folder to <samp><code>dimensions/minecraft/overworld</code></samp>
<ul><li>This includes the <samp><code>region</code></samp>, <samp><code>entities</code></samp>, and <samp><code>poi</code></samp> folders, as well as related files out of data.</li></ul></li>
<li>Data for the Nether has been moved from <samp><code>DIM-1</code></samp> to <samp><code>dimensions/minecraft/the_nether</code></samp></li>
<li>Data for the End has been moved from <samp><code>DIM1</code></samp> to <samp><code>dimensions/minecraft/the_end</code></samp></li>
<li>The top level <samp><code>data</code></samp> folder is now only for data shared across dimensions instead of also for the Overworld.</li></ul></li>
<li>Player storage has been moved to the <samp><code>players</code></samp> subdirectory.
<ul><li><samp><code>advancements</code></samp> → <samp><code>players/advancements</code></samp></li>
<li><samp><code>playerdata</code></samp> → <samp><code>players/data</code></samp></li>
<li><samp><code>stats</code></samp> → <samp><code>players/stats</code></samp></li></ul></li>
<li>The world resource pack (<samp><code>resources.zip</code></samp>) has been moved to the <samp><code>resourcepacks</code></samp> subdirectory.</li>
<li>Data saved in the <samp><code>data</code></samp> folder is now namespaced.
<ul><li>This means that all that data will now be stored in a namespace subfolder in the corresponding data folder.
<ul><li>All existing vanilla data files have been moved accordingly.</li>
<li>Example: <samp><code>data/scoreboard.dat</code></samp> → <samp><code>data/minecraft/scoreboard.dat</code></samp></li></ul></li>
<li>Command storage is now stored in namespace subfolders instead of having a namespace suffix.
<ul><li>Example: <samp><code>data/command_storage_foo.dat</code></samp> → <samp><code>data/foo/command_storage.dat</code></samp></li></ul></li>
<li><samp><code>chunks.dat</code></samp> has been renamed to <samp><code>chunk_tickets.dat</code></samp></li>
<li>Data for maps is now stored in the <samp><code>data/minecraft/maps</code></samp> subfolder.
<ul><li>Map index files have been renamed to only the number.
<ul><li>Example: <samp><code>map_1.dat</code></samp> → <samp><code>1.dat</code></samp></li></ul></li>
<li><samp><code>idcounts.dat</code></samp> has been renamed to <samp><code>last_id.dat</code></samp></li></ul></li>
<li>There is no more <samp><code>raids_end.dat</code></samp> special case.
<ul><li>The End now uses <samp><code>raids.dat</code></samp> as well.</li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li>Structures saved by Structure Blocks have been moved from <samp><code>generated/namespace/structures</code></samp> to <samp><code>generated/namespace/structure</code></samp></li></ul>
<p><b>Lightmap algorithm</b>
</p>
<ul><li>The algorithm that maps block and sky light levels to how bright things appear on screen has been fully rewritten.</li>
<li>A new algorithm that is supposed to mostly provide the same overall results as previous one, but:
<ul><li>It is simpler and more straightforward, and fixes multiple issues of the previous one.</li>
<li>The <a href="/w/Darkness" title="Darkness">darkness</a> effect and world darkening effect of the <a href="/w/Wither" title="Wither">Wither</a> fight now works the same way in all dimensions.</li>
<li>The <a href="/w/Night_vision" class="mw-redirect" title="Night vision">night vision</a> effect now simply adds ambient light instead of scaling the resulting colors.
<ul><li>It means that fully dark areas no longer look brighter than areas lit by block or sky light.</li></ul></li>
<li>Other aspects of the algorithm such as block light tint, ambient light color and night vision color are now data-driven through environment attributes.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b>Lightmap shader</b>
</p>
<ul><li>The <code>lightmap.fsh</code> shader was significantly modified.
<ul><li>The <code>LightmapInfo</code> uniform now has two new fields:
<ul><li><code>BlockLightTint</code></li>
<li><code>NightVisionColor</code></li></ul></li>
<li>The <code>AmbientLightFactor</code> field was removed, its value is now premultiplied into <code>AmbientColor</code></li>
<li>The <code>DarkenWorldFactor</code> was renamed to <code>BossOverlayWorldDarkeningFactor</code></li></ul></li>
<li>Text and items rendered in UI now use a separate 1x1 white lightmap texture, so the lightmap shader does not always have to keep the 15, 15 pixel purely white.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Loot_functions" class="mw-redirect" title="Loot functions">Loot functions</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:enchant_with_levels</code>
<ul><li>Now also takes the following field:
<ul><li><code>include_additional_cost_component</code> – optional boolean representing if a <code>minecraft:additional_trade_cost</code> component should be added to the item based on the cost of the enchantment.
<ul><li>Defaults to <code>false</code></li>
<li>The value is determined by the levels number provider and is the same that is used to determine what enchantment level is used for enchanting.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:enchant_randomly</code>
<ul><li>Now also takes the following field:
<ul><li><code>include_additional_cost_component</code> – optional boolean representing if a <code>minecraft:additional_trade_cost</code> component should be added to the item based on the cost of the enchantment.
<ul><li>Defaults to <code>false</code></li>
<li>The value is determined by the value selected by levels or its default value using the following formula: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">*</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">*</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>l</mi></mstyle></mrow></math></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:set_instrument</code>
<ul><li>The <code>options</code> field now also accepts an ID and a list of IDs in addition to a tag.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Loot_table" title="Loot table">Loot tables</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Removed the <a href="/w/Name_tag" class="mw-redirect" title="Name tag">name tag</a> from <a href="/w/Ancient_cities" class="mw-redirect" title="Ancient cities">ancient cities</a> and <a href="/w/Woodland_mansion" class="mw-redirect" title="Woodland mansion">woodland mansions</a>.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Mob_variant_definitions" title="Mob variant definitions">Mob variant definitions</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Wolf sound variants sound events in <code>wolf_sound_variant</code> have been moved into a new field <code>adult_sounds</code> and the field <code>baby_sounds</code> was added.</li></ul>
<p><b>Mob sound variant</b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added adult sound variants for the following animals:
<ul><li>Cats have a new variant called <code>royal</code>.</li>
<li>Pigs have new variants called <code>mini</code> and <code>big</code>.</li>
<li>Cows have a new variant called <code>moody</code>.</li>
<li>Chickens have a new variant called <code>picky</code>.</li>
<li>The original sounds of each animal are used for the variant called <code>classic</code>.</li>
<li>Every one of these animals will have a random sound variant assigned to it from the new variants and the original one.</li></ul></li>
<li><a href="/w/Cat" title="Cat">Cat</a> sound variants
<ul><li>Cat sound variants can be data-driven by adding entries to <code>data//cat_sound_variant/.json</code></li>
<li>The file contains two sound sets defining <code>adult_sounds</code> and <code>baby_sounds</code></li>
<li>Each sound set contains the following fields which correspond to sound events to use for the specific behavior:
<ul><li><code>ambient_sound</code></li>
<li><code>stray_ambient_sound</code></li>
<li><code>hiss_sound</code></li>
<li><code>hurt_sound</code></li>
<li><code>death_sound</code></li>
<li><code>eat_sound</code></li>
<li><code>beg_for_food_sound</code></li>
<li><code>purr_sound</code></li>
<li><code>purreow_sound</code></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><a href="/w/Pig" title="Pig">Pig</a> sound variants
<ul><li>Pig sound variants can be data-driven by adding entries to <code>data//pig_sound_variant/.json</code></li>
<li>The file contains two sound sets defining <code>adult_sounds</code> and <code>baby_sounds</code>.</li>
<li>Each sound set contains the following fields which correspond to sound events to use for the specific behavior:
<ul><li><code>ambient_sound</code></li>
<li><code>hurt_sound</code></li>
<li><code>death_sound</code></li>
<li><code>step_sound</code></li></ul></li>
<li>Eating sound customization is now supported through the new field <code>eat_sound</code> big variant sound sets.</li></ul></li>
<li><a href="/w/Cow" title="Cow">Cow</a> sound variants
<ul><li>Cow sound variants can be data-driven by adding entries to <code>data//cow_sound_variant/.json</code></li>
<li>Each sound variant contains the following fields which correspond to sound events to use for the specific behavior:
<ul><li><code>ambient_sound</code></li>
<li><code>hurt_sound</code></li>
<li><code>death_sound</code></li>
<li><code>step_sound</code></li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li><a href="/w/Chicken" title="Chicken">Chicken</a> sound variants
<ul><li>Chicken sound variants can be data-driven by adding entries to <code>data//chicken_sound_variant/.json</code></li>
<li>The file contains two sound sets defining <code>adult_sounds</code> and <code>baby_sounds</code>.</li>

<p><b><a href="/w/Options" title="Options">Options</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The difficulty button in the pause menu has been replaced with a button leading to a new screen – World Options.
<ul><li>The world options screen contains the difficulty button as well as a button for changing game rules.</li>
<li>The game rules screen is available for all operators and otherwise disabled.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Panorama" title="Panorama">Panorama</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Updated the panorama to reflect <a href="/w/Tiny_Takeover" title="Tiny Takeover">Tiny Takeover</a>.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Predicate" title="Predicate">Predicates</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Entity Predicates
<ul><li><code>player</code> Sub-Predicate
<ul><li>New optional field: <code>food</code></li>
<li>A Food predicate</li>
<li>Format: Object with fields:
<ul><li><code>level</code> – optional integer min/max range specifying the required food level.</li>
<li><code>saturation</code> – optional float min/max range specifying the required saturation level.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:time_check</code> loot predicate
<ul><li>Added <code>clock</code> field: a world clock ID, specifies which world clock the time check should be done for.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Recipe" class="mw-disambig" title="Recipe">Recipes</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li><code>result</code> field should now be more consistent across all recipe types that contain it.
<ul><li>It will now accept short form (e.g. "<code>minecraft:foo</code>", which is equivalent to <code>{"id":"minecraft:foo", "count": 1}</code>).</li>
<li>For recipe types <code>smelting</code>, <code>blasting</code>, <code>smoking</code> and <code>campfire_cooking</code> this field now also accepts <code>count</code> field.</li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_special_mapcloning</code> recipe type has been removed, functionality has been absorbed by <code>minecraft:crafting_transmute</code>.</li>
<li>New <code>show_notification</code> fields with the same functionality as existing one in <code>minecraft:crafting_shaped</code> have been added to the following existing recipe types:
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_shapeless</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:crafting_shaped</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:crafting_transmute</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:smelting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:blasting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:smoking</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:campfire_cooking</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:stonecutting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:smithing_transform</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:smithing_trim</code></li></ul></li>
<li>Removed unused <code>group</code> field from recipes without a recipe book:
<ul><li><code>minecraft:stonecutting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:smithing_transform</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:smithing_trim</code></li></ul></li>
<li>Renamed the following stonecutter recipes, along with the relevant advancement:
<ul><li><code>minecraft:chiseled_stone_bricks_stone_from_stonecutting</code> → <code>minecraft:chiseled_stone_bricks_from_stone_stonecutting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:end_stone_brick_slab_from_end_stone_brick_stonecutting</code> → <code>minecraft:end_stone_brick_slab_from_end_stone_bricks_stonecutting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:end_stone_brick_stairs_from_end_stone_brick_stonecutting</code> → <code>minecraft:end_stone_brick_stairs_from_end_stone_bricks_stonecutting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:end_stone_brick_wall_from_end_stone_brick_stonecutting</code> → <code>minecraft:end_stone_brick_wall_from_end_stone_bricks_stonecutting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:mossy_stone_brick_slab_from_mossy_stone_brick_stonecutting</code> → <code>minecraft:mossy_stone_brick_slab_from_mossy_stone_bricks_stonecutting</code></li>
