<li><code>minecraft:mossy_stone_brick_wall_from_mossy_stone_brick_stonecutting</code> → <code>minecraft:mossy_stone_brick_wall_from_mossy_stone_bricks_stonecutting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:prismarine_brick_slab_from_prismarine_stonecutting</code> → <code>minecraft:prismarine_brick_slab_from_prismarine_bricks_stonecutting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:prismarine_brick_stairs_from_prismarine_stonecutting</code> → <code>minecraft:prismarine_brick_stairs_from_prismarine_bricks_stonecutting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:quartz_slab_from_stonecutting</code> → <code>minecraft:quartz_slab_from_quartz_block_stonecutting</code></li>
<li><code>minecraft:stone_brick_walls_from_stone_stonecutting</code> → <code>minecraft:stone_brick_wall_from_stone_stonecutting</code></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_transmute</code>
<ul><li>Recipes with this type can now accept multiple items matched by the <code>material</code> ingredient.</li>
<li>Added fields:
<ul><li><code>material_count</code> – integer range describing the amount of items matched by the material ingredient.
<ul><li>Must be a subrange of <code>[1,8]</code></li>
<li>Default: <code>[1,1]</code> (i.e. exactly one item).</li></ul></li>
<li><code>add_material_count_to_result</code> – boolean field (default: <code>false</code>).
<ul><li>When <code>true</code>, the amount of slots containing items matched by the <code>material</code> ingredient will be added to the final count of the result.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_dye</code>
<ul><li>Replaces <code>minecraft:crafting_special_armordye</code></li>
<li>Output:
<ul><li>This recipe will first mix the current value of the <code>minecraft:dyed_color</code> component from the item matched by the target ingredient with the <code>minecraft:dye</code> component values from the items matched by the <code>dye</code> ingredients.</li>
<li>Result will be built by transmuting the item matched by the <code>target</code> ingredient into the <code>result</code> item stack and then applying the new value of the <code>minecraft:dyed_color</code> component.</li></ul></li>
<li>Fields:
<ul><li><code>category</code> – crafting book category, one of <code>building</code>, <code>redstone</code>, <code>equipment</code>, <code>misc</code>, default: <code>misc</code></li>
<li><code>group</code> – string value used for grouping recipes in the crafting book, default: empty string</li>
<li><code>show_notification</code> – optional boolean describing if a popup should be shown when this recipe is unlocked, default: <code>true</code></li>
<li><code>target</code> – ingredient (was harcoded to <code>#dyeable</code> tag).</li>
<li><code>dye</code> – ingredient (was <a href="/w/Java_Edition_hardcoded_item_properties" class="mw-redirect" title="Java Edition hardcoded item properties">hardcoded</a> to dye items).
<ul><li>The <code>minecraft:dye</code> component is required on matching items for the whole recipe to match.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>result</code> – resulting item stack (was always a copy of the item matched by the <code>target</code> ingredient).</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_imbue</code>
<ul><li>Replaces <code>minecraft:crafting_special_tippedarrow</code></li>
<li>Matches a single <code>source</code> ingredient surrounded by eight <code>material</code> ingredients</li>
<li>Output:
<ul><li><ul><li>This recipe will copy the <code>minecraft:potion_contents</code> component value from the item matched by the <code>source</code> ingredient to the resulting stack.</li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li>Fields:
<ul><li><code>category</code> – crafting book category, one of <code>building</code>, <code>redstone</code>, <code>equipment</code>, <code>misc</code>, default: <code>misc</code></li>
<li><code>group</code> – string value used for grouping recipes in the crafting book, default: empty string</li>
<li><code>show_notification</code> – optional boolean describing if a popup should be shown when this recipe is unlocked, default: <code>true</code></li>
<li><code>source</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:lingering_potion</code>)</li>
<li><code>material</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:arrow</code>)</li>
<li><code>result</code> – resulting item stack (was hardcoded to eight <code>minecraft:tipped_arrow</code>)</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_special_bannerduplicate</code>
<ul><li>Ingredients can now be restrained.</li>
<li>Output can now be configured.</li>
<li>The recipe still only works for banner items.</li>
<li>Removed unused <code>category</code> field.</li>
<li>Added fields:
<ul><li><code>banner</code> – ingredient to be used for both source and target items (was hardcoded to any banner item).</li>
<li><code>result</code> – resulting item stack (was always a copy of the Banner item with non-empty pattern).</li></ul></li>
<li>Output:
<ul><li>The recipe finds the first banner item matched by the <code>banner</code> ingredient and treats it as the source banner.</li>
<li>Result will be built by transmuting the source banner into the <code>result</code> item stack.</li>
<li>The source banner will be kept in the crafting grid.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_special_bookcloning</code>
<ul><li>Ingredients and output can now be configured.</li>
<li>Removed unused <code>category</code> field.</li>
<li>Added fields:
<ul><li><code>source</code> – ingredient to be used as a source book
<ul><li>The <code>minecraft:written_book_contents</code> component is required on the matching item for the whole recipe to match.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>material</code> – ingredient to target the item to be cloned (was hardcoded to <code>#book_cloning_target</code> tag).</li>
<li><code>allowed_generations</code> – integer range describing allowed value of the generation field of <code>minecraft:written_book_contents</code> component on the item matched by the material ingredient.
<ul><li>Must be a subrange of <code>[0,2]</code></li>
<li>Default: <code>[0,1]</code> (i.e. accepting original and first copies, but not copies of a copy).</li></ul></li>
<li><code>result</code> – resulting item stack (was always a copy of the item matched by the source ingredient).</li></ul></li>
<li>Output:
<ul><li>The recipe will first take the value of <code>minecraft:written_book_contents</code> component in the item matched by the <code>source</code> ingredient.</li>
<li>Field <code>generation</code> in <code>minecraft:written_book_contents</code> will be incremented by one.
<ul><li>The recipe will not yield a result if the value of <code>generation</code> is <code>2</code> or more.</li></ul></li>
<li>Result will be built by transmuting item matched by the <code>source</code> ingredient to the <code>result</code> item stack and then applying the new value of <code>minecraft:written_book_contents</code> component.</li>
<li>Number of items matched by the <code>material</code> ingredient beyond the first one will be added to the resulting stack size.</li>
<li>The original item matched by the <code>source</code> ingredient will be kept in the crafting grid.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_decorated_pot</code>
<ul><li>Ingredients and result can now be configured.</li>
<li>Removed unused <code>category</code> field.</li>
<li>Added fields:
<ul><li><code>back</code>, <code>left</code>, <code>right</code>, <code>front</code> – ingredients (was hardcoded to <code>#decorated_pot_ingredients</code>).</li>
<li><code>result</code> – resulting item stack (was hardcoded to a single <code>minecraft:decorated_pot</code>).</li></ul></li>
<li>Other functionality remains unchanged, i.e. items matched by ingredients will be added to the matching fields in the <code>minecraft:pot_decorations</code> component of the resulting stack.</li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_special_firework_rocket</code>
<ul><li>Ingredients and result can now be configured.</li>
<li>Removed unused <code>category</code> field.</li>
<li>Added fields:
<ul><li><code>shell</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:paper</code>).</li>
<li><code>fuel</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:gunpowder</code>).</li>
<li><code>star</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:firework_star</code>).</li>
<li><code>result</code> – resulting item stack (was hardcoded to three <code>minecraft:firework_rocket</code>).</li></ul></li>
<li>Output:
<ul><li>Exactly one stack matching the <code>shell</code> ingredient must be present.</li>
<li>The number of stacks matching the <code>fuel</code> ingredient will control the <code>flight_duration</code> field.</li>
<li>The <code>explosions</code> field will be copied from the <code>minecraft:firework_explosion</code> component of the <code>star</code> ingredient (if any).</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_special_firework_star_fade</code>
<ul><li>Ingredients can now be configured.</li>
<li>Removed unused <code>category</code> field.</li>
<li>The recipe will now use the <code>minecraft:dye</code> component instead of a hardcoded mapping of dye items to colors.</li>
<li>Added fields:
<ul><li><code>target</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:firework_star</code>).</li>
<li><code>dye</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to dye items).
<ul><li>The <code>minecraft:dye</code> component is required on matching items for the whole recipe to match.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>result</code> – resulting item stack (was always a copy of the item matched by the <code>target</code> ingredient).</li></ul></li>
<li>Output:
<ul><li>This recipe will find the current value of the <code>minecraft:firework_explosion</code> component from the item matched by the <code>target</code> ingredient.</li>
<li>The <code>fade_colors</code> field of the <code>minecraft:dye</code> component will be set to the values from the items matched by the <code>dye</code> ingredients.</li>
<li>Result will be built by transmuting item matched by the <code>target</code> ingredient into the <code>result</code> item stack and then applying the new value of <code>minecraft:firework_explosion</code> component.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_special_firework_star</code>
<ul><li>Ingredients and result can now be configured.</li>
<li>Removed unused <code>category</code> field.</li>
<li>Added fields:
<ul><li><code>trail</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:diamond</code>).</li>
<li><code>twinkle</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:glowstone_dust</code>).</li>
<li><code>fuel</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:gunpowder</code>).</li>
<li><code>dye</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to dye items).
<ul><li>The <code>minecraft:dye</code> component is required on matching items for the whole recipe to match.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>shapes</code> – a map of shapes to ingredients.
<ul><li>Allowed keys are the same as the ones for the <code>shape</code> field in the <code>minecraft:firework_explosion</code> component (i.e. <code>small_ball</code>, <code>large_ball</code>, <code>star</code>, <code>creeper</code>, <code>burst</code>).</li>
<li>Was hardcoded to: <code>minecraft:fire_charge</code> – <code>large_ball</code>, <code>minecraft:feather</code> – <code>burst</code>, <code>minecraft:gold_nugget</code> – star, any skull or head – <code>creeper</code></li></ul></li>
<li><code>result</code> – resulting item stack (was hardcoded to three <code>minecraft:firework_star</code>).</li></ul></li>
<li>The recipe will now use the <code>minecraft:dye</code> component instead of a hardcoded mapping of dye items to colors.</li>
<li>Output:
<ul><li>Exactly one stack matching the <code>fuel</code> ingredient must be present.</li>
<li>Result will be based on the <code>result</code> field, with the contents of the <code>minecraft:firework_explosion</code> component built with following values:
<ul><li>The values of the <code>minecraft:dye</code> component of items matched by the <code>dye</code> ingredient will be added to the <code>colors</code> field.</li>
<li>If an item matched by the <code>trail</code> ingredient is present, the <code>has_trail</code> field will be set to <code>true</code>.</li>
<li>If an item matched by the <code>twinkle</code> ingredient is present, the <code>has_twinkle</code> field will be set to <code>true</code>.</li>
<li>The <code>shape</code> field will be set based on the item matched by any of ingredients in the <code>shape</code> field (or <code>small_ball</code> if none is found).</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_special_mapextending</code>
<ul><li>Ingredients and output can now be configured.</li>
<li>Removed unused <code>category</code> field.</li>
<li>Added fields:
<ul><li><code>map</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:filled_map</code> with <code>minecraft:map_id</code> components).
<ul><li><code>minecraft:map_id</code> component is required on the matching map item for the whole recipe to match.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>material</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:paper</code>).</li>
<li><code>result</code> – resulting item stack (was always a copy of the item matched by the <code>map</code> ingredient).
<ul><li>If isn't a <code>minecraft:filled_map</code>, the game crashes or attempts to retrieve the item it from the crafting table, due to a lack of necessary post-processing<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>.</li></ul></li></ul></li>
<li>Output:
<ul><li>The recipe finds the item matched by the <code>map</code> ingredient with the <code>minecraft:map_id</code> component set.</li>
<li>Result will be built by transmuting the source item into the <code>result</code> item stack.</li>
<li><code>minecraft:map_post_processing</code> component will be set on the result item.</li>
<li>The source item will be kept in the crafting grid.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:crafting_special_shielddecoration</code>
<ul><li>Ingredients and output can now be configured.</li>
<li>Removed unused <code>category</code> field.</li>
<li>Added fields:
<ul><li><code>banner</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to any banner item).
<ul><li>Will only match if the item is a banner.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>target</code> – ingredient (was hardcoded to <code>minecraft:shield</code>).
<ul><li><code>minecraft:banner_patterns</code> component must be not set or be empty for the whole recipe to match.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>result</code> – resulting item stack (was always a copy of the item matched by the <code>target</code> ingredient).</li></ul></li>
<li>Functionality remains unchanged, i.e. this recipe will apply the following changes to the copy of the item matched by the <code>target</code> ingredient:</li>
<li>Output:
<ul><li>Result will be built by transmuting the item matched by the <code>target</code> ingredient into the <code>result</code> item stack and then:
<ul><li>Copying the <code>minecraft:banner_patterns</code> component from the item matched by the <code>banner</code> ingredient.</li>
<li>Setting the <code>minecraft:base_color</code> component based on the type of the banner matched by the <code>banner</code> ingredient.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Rendering" title="Rendering">Rendering</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Some changes have been made to the way blocks states render in places like enderman-held blocks, block display entities, etc. but not <a href="/w/Falling_block" class="mw-redirect" title="Falling block">falling blocks</a> or <a href="/w/Piston" title="Piston">pistons</a>.
<ul><li><a href="/w/Enchanting_table" class="mw-redirect" title="Enchanting table">Enchanting tables</a> will now show a closed book on the top of the block.</li>
<li>Blocks that use special renderers (like chests, banners, skulls) should now respect block state properties:
<ul><li>Rendering now respects the <code>rotation</code> and <code>facing</code> properties (where applicable).</li>
<li><a href="/w/Bed" title="Bed">Beds</a> now only render one half of the model, depending on the <code>part</code> property.</li>
<li><a href="/w/Copper_golem_statue" class="mw-redirect" title="Copper golem statue">Copper golem statues</a> will now respect the <code>copper_golem_pose</code> property.</li>
<li><a href="/w/Wall" title="Wall">Walls</a> and freestanding <a href="/w/Sign" title="Sign">signs</a>, <a href="/w/Hanging_sign" class="mw-redirect" title="Hanging sign">hanging signs</a>, <a href="/w/Banner" title="Banner">banners</a> and <a href="/w/Head" title="Head">heads</a> will now have separate models.</li>
<li><a href="/w/Chest" title="Chest">Chests</a> now respect part properties (where applicable).</li></ul></li>
<li>In general, all block states should look the same when rendered on a Block Display as they look when placed in world, except: fluids, end gateway, end portal.</li></ul></li>
<li><a href="/w/End_gateway" class="mw-redirect" title="End gateway">End gateway</a> and <a href="/w/End_portal" title="End portal">end portal</a> should now look the same when rendered on a <a href="/w/Block_display" class="mw-redirect" title="Block display">block display</a> as they look when placed in world.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/Resource_pack" title="Resource pack">Resource pack</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>The version is now <code>84.0</code>.</li>
<li>The glow particles emitted by glow squids, lightning rods, blocks being waxed, unwaxed and scraped is now rendered as opaque, since they never actually used translucency.</li>
<li>Removed <samp>demo_background.png</samp> in favor of <samp>popup/background.png</samp> sprite.</li>
<li>Updated <samp>mule_baby.png</samp> and <samp>donkey_baby.png</samp> to fit the model properly.</li>
<li>Updated textures for Pup to fix issues with overlapping textures.</li></ul>
<p><b>Shaders & Post-process Effects</b>
</p>
<ul><li>The <samp>core/rendertype_item_entity_translucent_cull</samp> shaders have been removed in favor of <samp>core/entity</samp></li>
<li>The <samp>core/rendertype_translucent_moving_block</samp> shaders have been removed in favor of <samp>core/block</samp>.</li>
<li>The <samp>core/rendertype_entity_alpha</samp> and <samp>core/rendertype_entity_decal</samp> shaders have been replaced by a DISSOLVE flag implemented by <samp>core/entity</samp></li>
<li>Rendering of items (in UI and in the world) has been split from the <samp>core/entity</samp> into new <samp>core/item</samp> shaders.</li>
<li>The <code>block.vsh</code> and <code>terrain.vsh</code> no longer receive the <code>Normal</code> vertex attribute.</li>
<li>Some small changes were to how various shaders sample the lightmap texture. This includes <code>core/entity.vsh</code>, <code>core/item.vsh</code>, <code>core/rendertype_leash.vsh</code>, <code>core/rendertype_text.vsh</code>, <code>core/rendertype_text_background.vsh</code>, <code>core/rendertype_text_intensity.vsh</code>, and <code>core/rendertype_translucent_moving_block.vsh</code>.</li></ul>

<p><b><a href="/w/Tag" class="mw-disambig" title="Tag">Tags</a></b>

<ul><li>Block Tags
<ul><li>Renamed the following tags for consistency:

<p><b><a href="/w/Text_component_format" title="Text component format">Text component format</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Components in server status messages (MotD) nested more than 16 times will now be discarded and replaced with an ellipsis.</li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:nbt</code>
<ul><li>Tags resolved with the <code>minecraft:nbt</code> text component when the <code>interpret</code> field is set to <code>false</code> are now pretty-printed instead of being flattened into a single <code>text</code> component.</li>
<li>Contents of the <code>nbt</code> and <code>block</code> fields are no longer silently rejected when parsing fails.</li>
<li>The field <code>entity</code> no longer accepts trailing data after a selector.</li>
<li>A new option called <code>plain</code> has been added to remove styling from pretty-printed text.
<ul><li>The <code>plain</code> and <code>interpret</code> options can't both be enabled at the same time.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:object</code>
<ul><li>Added a new optional field named <code>fallback</code> that contains a text component to be used when object component itself can't be displayed (for example when printing messages in server logs or during narration).</li>
<li>Objects of type <code>player</code> (player heads) no longer can be used in server status messages (MotD).
<ul><li>All components of that type will be replaced by a fallback text.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:selector</code>
<ul><li>The field <code>selector</code> no longer accepts trailing data after a selector.</li></ul></li></ul>

<p><b><a href="/w/Timeline" title="Timeline">Timelines</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Added a <code>clock</code> field: a world clock ID, specifies which world clock the timeline is tied to.
<ul><li>This field is required, but to match previous behavior the <code>minecraft:overworld</code> clock can be used</li></ul></li>
<li>Added an optional <code>time_markers</code> field, an optional map between namespaced Time Marker IDs and either an int or a Time Marker object.
<ul><li>Format:
<ul><li>Non-negative int, the tick that the time marker marks.</li>
<li>Or object with fields:
<ul><li><code>ticks</code>: int between <code>0</code> and <code>period_ticks</code>, the tick that the time marker marks.</li>
<li><code>show_in_commands</code>: optional boolean, specifies whether the Time Marker will show up in command suggestions.
<ul><li>Default: <code>false</code></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/UI" class="mw-redirect" title="UI">UI</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Worlds that need to be upgraded will now show Upgrade and Play instead of Play Selected World.
<ul><li>The Edit World and Re-Create World buttons are disabled until the world has been upgraded.</li></ul></li>
<li>When starting such a world, a new upgrade progress screen will be shown.</li>
<li>Added new UI sprites: <code>gui/sprites/widget/preedit.png</code> for IME preedit overlay background.</li>
<li>If there are no screens open, IME input will be cancelled.</li>
<li>IME will be opened when a text input gains focus and closed when a text input loses focus.</li>
<li><code>sound_cache</code> debug entry has been added.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/User_interface" class="mw-redirect" title="User interface">User interface</a></b>
</p>
<ul><li>Input Method Editors (IME) candidates will now be shown in-game (on supported platforms, currently Windows and macOS) above currently edited text field.</li>
<li>Fullscreen no longer uses exclusive mode.</li></ul>
<p><b><a href="/w/World_generation" title="World generation">World generation</a></b>
</p>

</div>
<ul><li>Rule-based block state providers have changed so that their <code>fallback</code> is optional and can be empty.
<ul><li>In such cases that an empty fallback is invoked, features that use them will not place anything.</li>
<li>Current configuration that uses a rule-based block state provider is the <code>state_provider</code> in the <code>disk</code> feature.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>forest_rock</code> configured feature has been renamed to <code>block_blob</code></li>
<li><code>block_blob</code> feature configuration has changed to support the following parameters:
<ul><li><code>state</code> – The block the rock is made out of.</li>
<li><code>can_place_on</code> – A block predicate that defines which blocks the rock can be placed on.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>ice_spike</code> configured feature has been renamed to <code>spike</code></li>
<li>spike feature configuration now supports the following parameters:
<ul><li><code>state</code> – The block the spike is made out of.</li>
<li><code>can_place_on</code> – A block predicate that defines which blocks the spike can be placed on.</li>
<li><code>can_replace</code> – A block predicate that defines which blocks the spike can replace.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>huge_red_mushroom</code> and <code>huge_brown_mushroom</code> feature configurations have a new parameter:
<ul><li><code>can_place_on</code> – A block predicate that defines which blocks the huge mushroom can be placed on.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>alter_ground</code> tree decorator configuration has changed so that <code>provider</code> is now a rule-based block state provider.</li>
<li><code>tree</code> feature configuration has replaced the <code>force_dirt</code> and <code>dirt_provider</code> parameters with a single <code>below_trunk_provider</code> rule-based block state provider:
<ul><li>Format:
<ul><li><code>fallback</code> – An optional block state provider.</li>
<li><code>rules</code> – A list of rules.
<ul><li><code>if_true</code> – A block predicate that checks the block position before providing the block.</li>
<li><code>then</code> – A block state provider.</li></ul></li>
<li>Default value:</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-json mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr"><pre><span></span><span class="nt">"below_trunk_provider"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"rules"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">            </span><span class="nt">"if_true"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">                </span><span class="nt">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:not"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">                </span><span class="nt">"predicate"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">                    </span><span class="nt">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:matching_block_tag"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">                    </span><span class="nt">"tag"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:cannot_replace_below_tree_trunk"</span>
<span class="w">                </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">            </span><span class="p">},</span>
<span class="w">            </span><span class="nt">"then"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">                </span><span class="nt">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:simple_state_provider"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">                </span><span class="nt">"state"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">                    </span><span class="nt">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"minecraft:dirt"</span>
<span class="w">                </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">            </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">        </span><span class="p">}</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="p">]</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</pre></div>
<ul><li>Any trees that previously used <code>force_dirt</code> have a <code>below_trunk_provider</code> that always provides a dirt block instead.</li>
<li>Block state providers now have a new type called <code>rule_based_state_provider</code>
<ul><li>This was previously a separately parsed type but is now instead a sub-type of block state providers.</li>
<li>They can now be used in any other feature configurations as a block state provider and are no longer unique to the disk feature.</li>
<li>Format:
<ul><li><code>fallback</code> – An optional block state provider</li>
<li><code>rules</code> – A list of rules
<ul><li><code>if_true</code> – A block predicate that checks the block position before providing the block</li>
<li><code>then</code> – A block state provider</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li>Flower features
<ul><li>Features spawned from Bone Meal are no longer restricted to the flower feature type, and instead controlled by the <code>#can_spawn_from_bone_meal</code> configured feature tag.</li>
<li>The <code>flower</code>, <code>flower_no_bonemeal</code>, and <code>random_patch</code> feature types have been removed.
<ul><li>Instead, patches can be expressed as a sequence of <code>count</code> and <code>random_offset</code> placement modifiers.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li>Int Providers
<ul><li>Added the <code>trapezoid</code> int provider
<ul><li>Selects a random value with a trapezoid distribution, similar to the <code>trapezoid</code> float provider.</li>
<li>Format: object with fields:
<ul><li><code>min</code>: integer, the minimum value to generate.</li>
<li><code>max</code>: integer, the maximum value to generate.</li>
<li><code>plateau</code>: integer, the width of the "plateau" of the distribution in which all values are equally likely to occur.
<ul><li>A value of <code>0</code> is equivalent to a triangle distribution.</li>
<li>A value of <code>max-min</code> is equivalent to a uniform distribution.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><code>count</code> placement modifier
<ul><li>The <code>count</code> field is now limited to a range of <code>0</code> to <code>4096</code> instead of the previous <code>256</code>.</li></ul></li></ul>

<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-302734" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-302734">MC-302734</a> – Zombie horses constantly move in and out of water and burn to death.</li>

<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-303125" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-303125">MC-303125</a> – Creepers can blow up after the player dies.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-303344" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-303344">MC-303344</a> – Tooltips for selected items in dialogs are displayed even when the item isn't being hovered over.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-303389" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-303389">MC-303389</a> – The ender dragon's velocity can be affected by attacks while perched.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-303403" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-303403">MC-303403</a> – Hanging sign block displays render dark and above other blocks and mobs.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-303684" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-303684">MC-303684</a> – Hoglins despawn when attached to a lead.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-303685" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-303685">MC-303685</a> – Zoglins despawn when attached to leads.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-303692" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-303692">MC-303692</a> – Debug overlay text has an indent when improved transparency is disabled.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-303749" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-303749">MC-303749</a> – Dolphins can despawn when attached to leads.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-303750" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-303750">MC-303750</a> – Squids & glow squids can despawn when attached to leads.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-304023" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-304023">MC-304023</a> – Redundant level data fixer files are saved in worlds' "data" folder.</li>

<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-304361" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-304361">MC-304361</a> – The heads of zombie nautiluses have a massive empty gap on the back.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-304446" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-304446">MC-304446</a> – Activating a stasis chamber with a sponge deletes the ender pearl.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-304599" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-304599">MC-304599</a> – Dolphins don't follow players riding nautiluses like in Bedrock Edition.</li>

<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-304683" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-304683">MC-304683</a> – Wandering traders don't spawn in single biome snowy plains worlds.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-304705" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-304705">MC-304705</a> – The E value in <code>entity_render_stats</code> in the debug overlay doesn't work.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-304725" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-304725">MC-304725</a> – Zombie villagers summoned with default spawn eggs always spawn as their plains variant.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-304761" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-304761">MC-304761</a> – Spears' charge animation takes too long to rotate sideways for slower spears.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-304796" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-304796">MC-304796</a> – Hovering over a disabled slider shows the pointing hand cursor instead of the forbidden cursor.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-304991" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-304991">MC-304991</a> – Clicking on a chest with loot that hasn't been generated in Spectator mode makes the "<code>block.chest.locked</code>" sound.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305012" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305012">MC-305012</a> – The description of the "Universal anger" game rule still uses the old ID of the "Forgive dead players" game rule.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305040" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305040">MC-305040</a> – Nautili spawned as a result of a player breeding two other nautili can despawn.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305123" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305123">MC-305123</a> – Curse of Vanishing doesn't work when the item is equipped on an armor stand.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305196" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305196">MC-305196</a> – Witches always miss their shots when close to their target.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305292" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305292">MC-305292</a> – Copper chests use the Christmas present texture.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305369" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305369">MC-305369</a> – Trying to attach a leash to a fence outside its reach places a ghost leash knot and plays a sound.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305388" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305388">MC-305388</a> – Bees never cease to be angry.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305471" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305471">MC-305471</a> – Cacti appear with seams on the edges and corners when using higher resolution texture packs with mipmaps enabled.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305580" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305580">MC-305580</a> – Baby zombie horses and baby skeleton horses grow into adults, unlike other baby undead mobs.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305699" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305699">MC-305699</a> – Piglins in groups fail to initiate hoglin hunting behavior.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305857" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305857">MC-305857</a> – Entity hitboxes now move jaggedly when the game is frozen.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-305888" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-305888">MC-305888</a> – Turtle eggs no longer hatch in the Nether or the End.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-306064" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-306064">MC-306064</a> – Mobs can be forced to look like they're dying while they aren't by using commands.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-306110" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-306110">MC-306110</a> – The side textures of black, white splotched, killer, and Toast rabbits' heads extend to the bottom of their heads.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-306123" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-306123">MC-306123</a> – Wolves still try to attack players even in Peaceful difficulty.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-306427" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-306427">MC-306427</a> – Certain mobs holding items with empty "<code>kinetic_weapon</code>" components crash the game whenever target acquisition succeeds.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-306566" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-306566">MC-306566</a> – The totem of undying screen effect now jitters while the game is frozen.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-306658" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-306658">MC-306658</a> – Dolphins will let themselves drown even with ample access to air.</li>
<li><a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-306798" class="extiw" title="mojira:MC-306798">MC-306798</a> – Ender dragons with a <code>DragonDeathTime</code> of 200 or greater never disappear.</li></ul>

metadata.description: 26.1, the release of Tiny Takeover, is a game drop for Java Edition released on March 24, 2026,[1] which adds new textures and models for every baby mob that did not already have a unique model, adds the golden dandelion, makes name tags craftable, makes technical changes, and fixes bugs.
